detailed_description: Character Frequency counts how often each character appears in pasted text. Paste or edit text in the input textarea, toggle Ignore Spaces and Case Sensitive checkboxes as needed, then click Analyze to run a local frequency count. The results panel shows the unique-character count, total character count, and a scrollable list where each row displays the character, a bar sized by its share of the maximum count, the count, and the percentage to one decimal place. It does not drag-and-drop files, choose Unicode normalization forms, compute entropy, render heatmaps, or export JSON or TSV files.
usage_steps: Paste or type text into the input textarea (a sample sentence is preloaded)
Tick Ignore Spaces to skip whitespace characters in the count
Tick Case Sensitive to treat uppercase and lowercase as different characters
Click Analyze to run the frequency count in the browser
Read the unique-character count and total-character count above the list
Scroll the result list to see each character with its bar, count, and percentage
usage_examples: Check which letters dominate a short paragraph while studying a substitution cipher
Compare the share of vowels and consonants in a sample of writing
Spot an unexpected character (for example a stray punctuation mark) inside a pasted snippet
See which glyphs are most common in a short UI string before designing an icon font sample

faqs.question: What can I use a character frequency analysis for?
faqs.answer: Common uses include solving substitution ciphers, comparing letter distribution in writing samples, spotting stray characters in pasted snippets, and checking glyph usage before font design.

faqs.question: What do the Ignore Spaces and Case Sensitive options do?
faqs.answer: Ignore Spaces excludes whitespace from the count, and Case Sensitive treats uppercase and lowercase letters as different characters. Both are off by default.

faqs.question: How are the percentages calculated?
faqs.answer: Each character's percentage is its count divided by the total counted characters, shown to one decimal place. Bars are sized relative to the most frequent character.

faqs.question: Is my text sent anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The frequency analysis runs locally in your browser, and your text never leaves the page.
